docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Global sporting-goods franchise with a channel problem
Source: https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm
Date: 2024-06-27

Nike designs and markets athletic footwear, apparel and equipment through wholesale partners and its own stores and digital channels. Manufacturing is principally outsourced. The company owns the Nike, Jordan and Converse brands. Scale is visible in revenue, athlete marketing and geographic distribution, but a large installed brand does not guarantee that each new product attracts consumers.

Fiscal 2024 revenue was $51,362 million, of which Nike Brand generated $49,322 million and Converse $2,082 million, with a small corporate reconciliation. Nike Brand footwear accounted for $33,427 million, apparel $13,775 million and equipment $2,075 million. Footwear is therefore the principal driver of product relevance and demand.

Nike Brand geographic revenue was $21,396 million North America, $13,607 million Europe/Middle East/Africa, $7,545 million Greater China and $6,729 million Asia Pacific/Latin America. A North American slowdown is important, but the franchise is not a single-country retailer.

Wholesale Nike Brand sales were $27,758 million; Nike Direct sales were $21,519 million. Direct selling offers customer data and the retail gross spread, but requires stores, fulfillment, technology, returns processing and demand acquisition. Wholesale sacrifices part of the retail margin while supplying distribution, shelf presence and consumer discovery. A higher direct mix is not automatically better if digital demand weakens or partner relationships deteriorate.

Annual gross margin was 44.6%. Company-defined EBIT was $6,539 million, or 12.7% of sales, after central brand and corporate expenses. Geographic segment EBIT should not be treated as fully allocated company earnings. Nike spent $4,285 million on demand creation, reflecting the ongoing cost of sustaining brand desirability.

John Donahoe is president and CEO; Matthew Friend is CFO. No change in chief executive is announced in the information supplied. The quarter's basic weighted-average common shares were 1,508.0 million and diluted shares 1,516.7 million.

The underwriting question is whether product innovation, balanced distribution and cost discipline can restore growth without damaging brand equity. Financial scale and liquidity provide room to act, but do not identify the correct product assortment or establish a recovery timetable.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Financial history before the new revenue reset
Source: compiled from: https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_downloads/2023/414759-1-_5_Nike-NPS-Combo_Form-10-K_WR.pdf; https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm
Date: 2024-06-27

Nike's fiscal year ends May 31. Figures below are the fiscal years publicly reported by June 28; no July 2024 annual report is used.

| Metric | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue, $m | 44,538 | 46,710 | 51,217 | 51,362 |
| Revenue growth | 19% | 5% | 10% | approximately flat |
| Gross margin | 44.8% | 46.0% | 43.5% | 44.6% |
| Diluted EPS | $3.56 | $3.75 | $3.23 | $3.73 |
| Operating cash flow, $m | 6,657 | 5,188 | 5,841 | Not in June release |

The fiscal 2024 EPS increase is not equivalent to a restoration of revenue growth. Net income was $5,700 million, up 12%, while the effective tax rate declined to 14.9% from 18.2%. EPS also benefits from lower average shares. Restructuring charges reduced annual EPS by $0.22; the release's non-GAAP EPS excluding those charges was $3.95.

Latest-quarter revenue was $12,606 million, down 2%; gross margin was 44.7%, up 110 basis points. Company-defined EBIT margin was 13.3%, compared with 9.5%. Quarterly diluted EPS was $0.99 and net income $1,500 million. Improved freight costs, pricing and lower overhead helped earnings despite sales weakness.

At May 31, cash and equivalents were $9,860 million and short-term investments $1,722 million. Current debt was $1,000 million, long-term debt $7,903 million and notes payable $6 million. Simple financial net cash is therefore approximately $2.673 billion, calculated, before operating leases. Inventories fell 11% to $7,519 million.

Annual dividends were $2.2 billion and buybacks $4.3 billion, retiring 41.4 million shares. Full-year 2024 FCF and cash capex are not supplied in the June release and are not backfilled from the later annual filing. The prior audited history is available for analysis; a matching four-year ROIC series is not recovered.

The company can fund repairs without an obvious immediate liquidity crisis. The harder question is normalized earnings when classic products are reduced and new demand has not yet replaced them.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: June results expose a deeper transition
Source: compiled from: https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm; https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/nike-expects-sales-declines-attempts-comeback-rcna159412
Date: 2024-06-28

Nike reported fiscal Q4 and annual results on June 27 after the market close. Q4 revenue declined 2% reported to $12.6 billion and was flat in constant currency. Nike Direct revenue fell 8% to $5.1 billion; digital fell 10%, and owned stores fell 2%. Wholesale revenue increased 5% reported and 8% currency neutral to $7.1 billion.

Converse revenue declined 18% to $480 million. Nike Brand revenue was $12.1 billion, down 1% reported, with currency-neutral gains outside North America partly offsetting North American weakness. This is broader than a single delayed shipment or isolated foreign-exchange issue.

Gross margin rose 110 basis points to 44.7%, helped by strategic pricing, lower ocean freight and logistics costs, and lower warehousing expense. Lower Nike Direct margins and currency partly offset the benefit. Selling and administrative expenses declined 7% to $4.1 billion. Earnings therefore look healthier than the current sales trajectory.

Donahoe said: “We are taking our near-term challenges head-on, while making continued progress in the areas that matter most to NIKE's future – serving the athlete through performance innovation, moving at the pace of the consumer and growing the complete marketplace.”

Friend said: “While we are encouraged by our progress, our fourth quarter results highlighted challenges that have led us to update our Fiscal '25 outlook.” That statement accompanies a material change in the forward sales baseline, not just caution about a single quarter.

CNBC's June 28 report, carried by NBC News, says Nike now expects fiscal 2025 sales down mid-single digits, compared with analyst expectations of a 0.9% increase. First-half revenue is expected down high single digits, versus the earlier low-single-digit decline outlook. The report also describes expected Q1 revenue down approximately 10%.

The repair plan prioritizes performance innovation and a more balanced marketplace, but the revenue bridge is uncertain. Analysts must not capitalize fiscal 2024 EPS as if the new guidance had no profit consequences. Equally, the release does not establish permanent loss of Nike's brand or balance-sheet capacity. Both the severity and duration of the reset require underwriting.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: June 28 closing price after the guidance shock
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NKE?period1=1687996800&period2=1719619200&interval=1d; https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nikes-downbeat-outlook-drags-jd-sports-puma-briefly-lifts-adidas-2024-06-28
Date: 2024-06-28

Yahoo's date-bounded daily price series gives a June 28 unadjusted close of $75.37, with volume of 129,967,000 shares. The one-year observation window from June 29, 2023 through June 28, 2024 has an intraday high of $123.39 and low of $74.55. The closing price is approximately 38.9% below the high, calculated. Reuters describes the session's fall as approximately 20%.

Average daily volume over that window was approximately 9.37 million shares, calculated from the source series. The earnings-shock session traded roughly fourteen times that average. Liquidity therefore supports institutional execution, but extraordinary volume is not evidence that fundamental risk has cleared.

At the close, trailing fiscal 2024 GAAP P/E is 20.2 times, calculated as $75.37 divided by $3.73 EPS. Using the company's $3.95 EPS excluding restructuring gives 19.1 times. Those are trailing measures. They do not incorporate the newly forecast fiscal 2025 sales decline or any further spending needed to regain product relevance.

Applying the quarter's basic weighted-average 1,508.0 million shares gives illustrative equity capitalization of $113.66 billion. This is not an exact point-in-time capitalization because average shares differ from shares outstanding at the close. Subtracting the reported approximately $2.673 billion financial net cash gives illustrative enterprise value of approximately $110.98 billion, before leases. Dividing by fiscal 2024 company-defined EBIT of $6.539 billion gives approximately 17.0 times trailing EV/EBIT, not EV/EBITDA.

A verified same-day forward consensus EPS, EV/EBITDA multiple, historical five-to-ten-year forward-multiple range and S&P 500 forward P/E are not recovered. Fiscal 2024 FCF is not yet available from the dated release, so no unsupported FCF yield is calculated.

The valuation question is therefore explicit: how much earnings decline and repair spending can the current price absorb? A lower multiple on an earnings base that is about to fall can be misleading. Conversely, a durable franchise with depressed earnings can look expensive on immediate profits while offering attractive long-term returns if repair succeeds.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: The market questions product relevance and the direct strategy
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nikes-downbeat-outlook-drags-jd-sports-puma-briefly-lifts-adidas-2024-06-28; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-plots-100-and-less-sneakers-lure-price-conscious-shoppers-2024-06-28; https://www.nbcnews.com/business/consumer/nike-expects-sales-declines-attempts-comeback-rcna159412
Date: 2024-06-28

Reuters on June 28 describes a surprise annual sales decline intensifying concern over Nike's ability to arrest market-share losses to newer brands. The critical issue is not simply an economic slowdown: competitors are attracting consumers while Nike deliberately reduces some older franchises and tries to accelerate innovation.

CNBC's June 28 report contrasts a new mid-single-digit annual revenue decline outlook with the market's expectation for modest growth. The size of the forecast revision raises questions about management's visibility and the duration of the repair. Strong Q4 gross margin does not settle those questions, because pricing and freight benefits can coexist with an eroding sales base.

Reuters's separate June 28 report says Nike plans a new range of shoes priced at $100 and below around the world. This acknowledges the importance of value-sensitive consumers. The opportunity is to broaden demand without sacrificing brand positioning. The risk is that lower price points or a greater need for promotions reduce the profitability of regained volume.

The channel dispute is equally important. Selling directly can look attractive in a spreadsheet because it captures the retailer's margin. Yet it can weaken wholesale relationships, reduce shelf presence and expose Nike to the full operating cost of digital fulfillment and stores. Q4 Direct revenue down 8% while wholesale grows 5% is consistent with a need to rebalance; it does not demonstrate that the full fix is already in place.

The bear scenario is that lost share reflects persistent product and cultural relevance problems rather than temporary inventory or distribution mistakes. In that case, rebuilding sales requires more marketing, lower prices and sustained innovation spending, limiting the recovery in earnings.

The constructive scenario is that the brand, athlete relationships and global scale survive a period of execution errors, with wholesale repair and new products restoring demand. Neither scenario assumes a CEO change: John Donahoe remains in charge as of June 28.

No verified dated sell-side target-price table is supplied. The sourced market concern is the revision in revenue expectations and competitive position, not an invented consensus prediction of a completed turnaround.
docs.D06_peer_industry.md:
Title: Competition is broader than the traditional sporting-goods duopoly
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nikes-downbeat-outlook-drags-jd-sports-puma-briefly-lifts-adidas-2024-06-28; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1858985/000185898524000014/ex991pressreleasedatedmarc.htm; https://www.adidas-group.com/en/media/press-releases/adidas-performs-better-than-expected-in-transition-year-2023; https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm
Date: 2024-06-28

Nike competes with Adidas and Puma across sportswear, with Hoka and On in performance running, and with a broad assortment of lifestyle brands. Reuters's June 28 report explicitly links the sales outlook to concern about share losses to newer competitors. Investors should therefore avoid assuming that the only alternative to Nike is an incumbent global brand with similar economics.

The immediate numeric benchmark available in the pack is Nike's own channel and segment history:

| Metric | Prior comparable period | Latest |
|---|---:|---:|
| Q4 Nike Direct revenue | Base period | down 8% reported |
| Q4 wholesale revenue | Base period | up 5% reported |
| Annual company gross margin | 43.5% | 44.6% |
| Annual company EBIT margin | 12.1% | 12.7% |
| Annual Converse sales | $2.427bn | $2.082bn |

On's March12 release reports2023 revenue of CHF1.7921billion, up46.6%, gross margin59.6% and adjusted EBITDA margin15.5%. It guided at least30% constant-currency2024 growth. Adidas's March13 release reports2023 revenue EUR21.427billion, down4.8% reported, with47.5% gross margin. These are dated fiscal comparisons, not June28 consensus. Different currencies, scale, calendars and channel mix limit comparability. Matching forward multiples were not recovered; no current screen is substituted.

Industry structure provides both protection and risk. Athlete sponsorships, global marketing, design capability and distribution scale are costly to replicate across categories. However, a focused challenger can enter a narrower running or lifestyle niche without replicating Nike's complete platform. The ability to win a category with a small assortment makes aggregate market share less secure than total revenue size suggests.

Wholesale retailers are both partners and gatekeepers. They can redirect shelf space and recommendations toward products customers want, which means restoring those relationships can matter as much as adding direct digital traffic. A balanced route to market may be more profitable than maximizing direct share at every cost.

The relevant peer comparison is consequently not just P/E. It is growth in newer products, full-price sell-through, promotional intensity, distribution access and marketing efficiency. Those operating indicators would help distinguish a repairable execution gap from structural brand-share loss. The pack does not contain a complete measured series for them, so the decision must retain uncertainty rather than treating scale as proof of immunity.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: Successive warnings and the June reset
Source: compiled from: https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-beats-quarterly-revenue-estimates-discounts-draw-demand-2024-03-21; https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/nike-shares-skid-switch-newer-styles-squeeze-revenue-2024-03-22; https://investors.nike.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/24/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2024-third-quarter-results; https://investors.nike.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000320187-24-000028/q4fy24exhibit991er.htm
Date: 2024-06-28

Fiscal 2023, reported in June 2023: revenue grew 10% to $51.217 billion, but gross margin was 43.5%, below fiscal 2022's 46.0%. This supplied a high sales base but weaker profitability as inventory and marketplace adjustments affected the business.

March 21, 2024: Nike's fiscal Q3 release reported $12.429 billion revenue, approximately flat, with Direct revenue approximately flat and digital down 3% reported. Wholesale revenue grew 3%. Inventory fell 13%, indicating progress on excess stock without a corresponding restoration of strong demand growth.

March 21–22, 2024: Reuters reported management expecting first-half fiscal 2025 revenue to decline by a low-single-digit percentage as Nike reduced older product franchises. Shares fell approximately 8% on March 22. This warning already established that a product transition could depress sales before the June report.

During fiscal 2024: Nike undertook organizational restructuring. The June release records $379 million of annual restructuring charges, mainly associated with streamlining the organization. Cost reductions can improve efficiency, but they are not a substitute for a successful product cycle.

June 27, 2024: full-year revenue was nearly flat at $51.362 billion. Q4 Direct revenue declined 8%, digital fell 10% and Converse declined 18%. Gross margin and EPS improved, illustrating the divergence between near-term profitability and weakening sales momentum.

June 27 earnings discussion, reported June 28: fiscal 2025 revenue outlook changed to a mid-single-digit decline; the first-half decline outlook deepened to high single digits. Management emphasized innovation and a balanced marketplace. No completed operational turnaround is established.

June 28, 2024: shares closed at $75.37 after an approximately 20% fall, on nearly 130 million shares. The market is repricing both earnings and confidence in the recovery timetable.

The timeline ends on that trading day. There is no announced CEO replacement, activist campaign by a new outside owner, or subsequent fiscal-quarter evidence in the pack. Any thesis requiring a specific future executive or a particular future product hit is conditional, not a fact available at this cutoff.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Pre-disclosure investment framework and portfolio
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2024/03/22201541/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2023-Annual-Report.pdf; https://13f.info/13f/000117266124002519-pershing-square-capital-management-l-p-q1-2024
Date: 2024-05-15

The latest public annual report is Pershing Square Holdings' March 22 report for 2023. PSH net assets were $12.06 billion at year-end, and cash and equivalents were approximately $1.929 billion. These are PSH figures, not total firm AUM or a June 28 cash balance. Exact firm AUM is not independently recovered in this source set.

The most recent available 13F is the March 31 quarter, filed May 15. The publicly discussed core portfolio includes Alphabet, Chipotle, Restaurant Brands International, Hilton, Canadian Pacific Kansas City and Howard Hughes. Universal Music Group and OTC Fannie/Freddie are important economic holdings not captured by an ordinary US listed-equity table. Exact comparable weights from this filing are unavailable in the recovered materials.

As a separately dated fund-level reference, December2023 PSH NAV weights were Universal Music24.88% directly, Alphabet14.06%, Chipotle13.71%, Restaurant Brands approximately13.50%, Hilton12.15%, Howard Hughes11.72% and Canadian Pacific8.70%. Additional Universal Music affiliate exposure and fund financing mean these weights should not be treated as a complete unlevered allocation or June2024 positions.

The annual report presents a concentrated, long-term strategy focused on high-quality businesses with durable competitive advantages and capable management. The restaurant, hotel-franchise, rail and music holdings illustrate the preference for strong brands, pricing or network advantages and a long runway for cash generation. Portfolio membership is not proof that a new candidate meets the same criteria.

Nike's global scale and outsourced manufacturing can fit a brand-franchise framework. The difficult exception is earnings predictability during a product/channel reset. A decision must distinguish the durability of the trademark from the durability of earnings at the current margin and sales base.

No verified current Nike-specific Ackman statement dated by June 28 is supplied. Nor does the pack disclose a private investment decision or an unreported current position. A new-position replay must reason from public fundamentals and the manager's prior principles, not from knowledge of later filings.

A complete recent-exit schedule, current cash balance and exact position limits are not recovered. They should be treated as unknown rather than inferred from 13F omissions. The 13F does not disclose all foreign holdings, OTC securities, cash, swaps or hedges.

For a concentrated manager, operational repair risk argues for explicit downside cases and sizing discipline. A large share-price fall may improve prospective returns, but uncertainty about the depth of the revenue reset can simultaneously reduce justified conviction.

drivers.driver: Nike's global brand and scale remain valuable despite operational underperformance.
Innovation and repair of wholesale distribution can restore demand.
Elliott Hill's operating knowledge strengthens the management repair thesis after September appointment, not at initial purchase.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: June28 is a requested alternative scenario after actual initiation. No Hill or later tariff information leaks into pack. Initial sizing approximate. Compendium places options conversion in early2025; year-end2024 common shares were 18.8m. Forward consensus, peer valuation table and exact firm AUM missing. FY24 FCF excluded because not supplied in dated June release.

valuation.eps_path: Recovery to $5.20 - $5.60 EPS in 3-5 years via margin expansion and revenue re-acceleration
valuation.downside_case: Limited by $2.673B net cash and dominant market position; terminal multiple contraction if innovation fails.

drivers.driver: The company remains the dominant global leader in athletic footwear and apparel with an unmatched competitive moat through athlete sponsorships, design, and scale [D01, D06].
The recent 20% sell-off and 38.9% cumulative drawdown represent a market overreaction to fixable operational errors rather than a terminal loss of brand relevance [D03, D04, D05].
We see a clear path to margin expansion and earnings growth by re-balancing the wholesale-DTC channel mix and refining the innovation pipeline [D05, D06].
The company’s balance sheet, featuring $9.86B in cash and $2.673B in net cash, provides significant flexibility to fund the turnaround and support EPS through buybacks [D02].

kill_criteria: Innovation pipeline fails to regain consumer mindshare for more than 18 months
EBIT margins continue to contract below 10% after fiscal 2025
Net cash position is significantly depleted by non-accretive capital allocation
Management fails to restore wholesale partnerships, leading to further sustained revenue decay
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the brand's loss of product relevance is structural and permanent, rendering the global scale insufficient to compete with agile, new entrants.
final.memo:
The Company is a preeminent global consumer franchise with an unrivaled competitive moat in athletic footwear and apparel, underpinned by its deep athlete roster, design prowess, and massive distribution scale [D01, D06]. Despite recent headwinds, it remains the dominant player in its category, generating high free cash flow and maintaining a balance sheet with $2.673 billion in net cash [D01, D02].

We believe the current market panic, triggered by a 20% single-day sell-off following guidance downgrades, is misguided [D03, D04]. The market has conflated temporary operational missteps—specifically a flawed over-reliance on direct-to-consumer channels and an innovation lull—with a permanent erosion of brand equity [D03, D05]. We view this dislocation as a classic opportunity to acquire a high-quality compounder at an attractive entry multiple of 19.1x [D04].

Our investment thesis relies on management successfully re-balancing the channel strategy to prioritize wholesale relationships and refocusing the innovation pipeline [D05, D06]. By optimizing the $4.285 billion annual demand creation spend and tightening operational execution, we see a path toward mid-teens EPS growth as EBIT margins recover from their current 12.7% toward historical peaks [D01, D06].

We intend to engage in a quiet, constructive dialogue with the Board to ensure these operational improvements are implemented promptly [D03, D05]. Given the current valuation, we believe the risk-reward is highly asymmetric, with a target IRR of 28% in our bull case [D04]. We are initiating a position with an 8% target allocation, confident that the underlying strength of the brand will prevail as the turnaround takes hold.

valuation.eps_path: Recovery from projected FY25 decline to ~$4.50 EPS by years 3-5
valuation.downside_case: Permanent loss of market share to niche competitors leading to structural margin compression.

drivers.driver: Nike is a dominant, globally recognized franchise with unparalleled scale in athletic footwear and apparel [D01].
The 20% single-day price decline has created an attractive entry point at ~20x earnings for a business with high brand equity [D04].
Current underperformance is driven by fixable execution errors in product innovation and channel strategy rather than structural obsolescence [D05].
Our engagement will focus on recalibrating the innovation pipeline and restoring the wholesale partnership model to regain growth [D05].

kill_criteria: Management fails to reset the product innovation pipeline to reverse market share losses within 18 months
Unit revenue growth remains negative for four consecutive quarters beyond FY25
Management pursues large, value-destructive M&A to artificially inflate growth
Operating margins continue to contract due to irreversible loss of pricing power and structural brand dilution
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the competitive inroads made by Hoka and On represent a permanent shift in consumer preference that Nike's innovation engine cannot overcome.
final.memo:
Nike remains one of the world's most dominant and recognizable consumer franchises, possessing a scale and brand equity that few competitors can replicate [D01]. Despite recent headwinds, the company maintains a robust balance sheet and generates significant cash flows, allowing it to navigate periods of transition without external capital dependency [D02].

The current market dislocation, highlighted by a 20% single-day decline in share price, stems from a palpable panic regarding FY25 guidance and perceived competitive losses [D03], [D04]. We believe the market incorrectly views these challenges as a permanent structural impairment [D05]. In our view, Nike is suffering from identifiable, fixable strategic missteps regarding product innovation and channel distribution, which have temporarily obscured the underlying strength of its brand [D05].

At a 20.2x P/E multiple, we are able to acquire a stake in a high-quality, globally dominant business at a discount to its historical premium [D04]. As management recalibrates its product development cycle and balances its direct-to-consumer strategy with a revitalized wholesale presence, we expect a return to mid-single-digit revenue growth and operating margin expansion [D05]. We view an exit multiple of 22x as appropriate for a restored, top-tier consumer compounder [D01].

Our role will be to engage privately and constructively with the Board and management to ensure these strategic pivots are prioritized [D05]. We intend to monitor the innovation pipeline closely, ensuring that the company's product offering regains its historical dominance in performance footwear [D05].

The primary risk to our thesis is that the competitive landscape has fundamentally changed, rendering Nike's current innovation pace insufficient [D05]. Should we conclude that the brand has lost its durability, we would exit the position. For now, the combination of a strong balance sheet, an iconic brand, and a clear path to execution-led recovery justifies an 8% position in the portfolio.
